title: Law to place financial literacy advisors in senior centers
summary: This bill would require the Department for the Aging to assign at least one financial literacy advisor to each older adult center for at least 20 hours a month. Advisors would give seniors general information on financial planning, end-of-life preparation, taxes and common scams, and connect them with specialized providers and city resources. The Commissioner would set advisor qualifications and create a training program, and the law would take effect 120 days after enactment.
